### **Job Description and Duties**


The dynamic, multi\-disciplinary FMO team is actively building new, creative solutions to long\-term regulatory challenges. You will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and experience to advance the environmental permitting for flood maintenance projects at a landscape level. Working within all facets of the projects such as design and budgeting, you will assist with advance mitigation concepts, environmental planning activities, monitoring, environmental assessment, and biological surveys. FMO offers direct networking and consultation opportunities with regulatory agency staff as you support complex environmental compliance for Sacramento River Flood Control Project maintenance activities, including channel rehabilitation, levee maintenance, and vegetation management. FMO is looking for someone who is highly motivated to find environmental solutions to flood management, takes initiative, and is team oriented. The incumbent should possess interpersonal, project management, organizational, oral and written communication skills.

jobs.title: Staff Environmental Geologist / Scientist / Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us:

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long\-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.  

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow\-through of an industry leader.  

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.
Overview:

TRC is seeking a highly motivated and detail\-oriented staff\-level Environmental Geologist, Scientist, or Civil Engineer to join our Engineering, Construction, and Remediation practice in Concord or Rancho Cordova, CA. The position focuses on a candidate seeking to develop technical skills to support various environmental consulting services, including environmental assessment/inspection, construction monitoring, data analysis, and reporting. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of task/project managers, integrate with our diverse regional team, and demonstrate motivation to support various field and technical efforts
Responsibilities:
* Assist in conducting environmental site assessments and investigations.
* Support remediation planning and implementation activities.
* Prepare work plans, technical reports, proposals, and health \& safety plans.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver project objectives.
* Conduct fieldwork, including soil/rock logging, sampling (soil, groundwater, soil vapor, air), monitoring, and inspections, in accordance with written plans and procedures.
* Coordinate with subcontractors and vendors to procure resources for and oversee fieldwork.
* Perform storm water inspections and sampling for construction, industrial, and municipal sites.
* Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal environmental regulations.
* Maintain accurate project documentation and data management.


Qualifications:
* Bachelor's degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field.
* 3\-7 years of relevant experience in environmental consulting or related areas.
* Experience with field data collection methods, including electronic collection of field observations, soil/rock logging, and soil/water/air sampling.
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
* Responsibility and accountability to perform assigned tasks to completion.
* Ability to learn through on\-the\-job experience and retain knowledge for progressive development.
* Proficiency with MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
* Willingness to travel for fieldwork and project assignments (up to approximately 50% local travel).
* Valid driver’s license required.
* Must be able to pass a pre\-employment background check, drug screen, physical and motor vehicle records check.
* Must have ability to lift 25 pounds.
* OSHA 40\-hour HAZWOPER certification, including current annual refresher
* Experience with data analysis and reporting
* Familiarity with environmental sampling procedures
* Engineer\-in\-Training (EIT) or Geologist\-in\-Training (GIT) certification
* Knowledge of California environmental regulations and permitting processes
* Experience with AutoCAD or GIS

  

\#LI\-SE1  

Benefits\*: TRC offers a competitive benefit package consisting of:* Medical, dental, vision, and disability insurance.
* 401k package that includes both traditional and Roth IRA options and Company match.
* Paid time off contingent upon full time or part time status and level of seniority (ranging from 15 to 25 days per year).
* All full\-time employees enjoy a minimum of 8 Paid Holidays per year.
* TRC ensures that all employees, including those that work part\-time, receive paid sick, family, and disability leave in accordance with the laws of their state of residence.
* These benefits are applicable to US employees depending on their employment status (full time, part time, or temporary). TRC offers jurisdiction specific benefit packages for International and Puerto Rico employees.

  

Compensation: In accordance with local law, the below salary range is applicable for the job and location associated with this requisition. Compensation will vary based upon experience, education, skill level, geographical location, and other compensable factors.  

Other Compensation: Employee may be eligible for participation in the Company’s annual Discretionary Bonus Program which is contingent on Company, Business Segment, and Individual performance against Key Performance Indicators which vary by year and employee.

jobs.description:
**Environmental Scientist/Engineer \- Journeyman**

We are looking for Senior Environmental Scientist/Engineer to assist with the U.S. Air Force’s Environmental Restoration Program. This support will provide Advisory and Assistance (A\&AS) services to AFCEC/CZO and CZR.  



**Compensation \& Benefits:**

Estimated Starting Salary Range for **Environmental Scientist/Engineer \- Journeyman** :


Pay commensurate with experience.


Full\-time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided. Benefits are subject to change with or without notice.  



**Environmental Scientist/Engineer \- Journeyman Responsibilities Include:**

* Provide specialized advisory and assistance (A\&AS) support services to the Air Force including:
	+ Air Force environmental restoration program management processes
	+ Environmental investigation and remediation contract oversight
	+ Safety briefings and accompanying remediation contractors into controlled areas and providing controlled area safety briefings.
	+ Development of statements of work and independent government estimates for environmental investigation and remediation contracts
	+ Reviewing investigation and remediation contractor’s deliverables including work plans, investigation reports, and recurring performance reports
	+ Conducting data gap analysis using ERPIMS data and submitting Data Gap reports
	+ Developing and refining current year and outyear project requirements to move sites toward site closure.
	+ Reviewing environmental investigation and remediation project schedules
	+ Updating Management Action Plans, Community Relations Plans, and other general Installation documents with the latest site cleanup information and status
* Assist with technical presentations to Air Force stakeholders in coordination with a variety of project stakeholders.
* Management of technical teams to include workload distribution and timely deliverable submittals.
* Interaction and correspondence with installation and AFCEC program managers
Performs other job\-related duties as assigned.  
* 

**Environmental Scientist/Engineer \- Journeyman Experience, Education, Skills, Abilities requested:**

* A bachelor's degree from an accredited discipline university in an Engineering or Scientific Discipline or related field is required. Substitution for master’s degree based on experience.
* Three (3\) to ten (10\) years of experience in environmental restoration accomplished under the Resource Conservation \& Recovery Act (RCRA) and the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (CERCLA)
* Performance Based Remediation (PBR) and Optimized Remediation Contracts (ORC) experience with one or more Federal agencies
* Experience with contract acquisition process including a variety of contract vehicles such as Air Force, GSA and USACE
* Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations, Defense Environmental Restoration Program (DERP) and Federal Acquisition Regulations including investigation of sites, site cleanup, and site closure.
* Experience interacting with state and federal environmental regulatory agencies preferred.
* Strong organizational skills and excellent communication skills both oral and written.
* Experience using Microsoft Office products including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
* Ability to multitask and meet aggressive deadlines.
* U.S. Citizenship and DoD government security clearance NACI required,
* Applicants selected will be subject to a U.S. Government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements,
Must pass pre\-employment qualifications of Cherokee Federal.  
* 

**Company Information:**

**Cherokee Nation Strategic Programs (CNSP)** is a part of Cherokee Federal – the division of tribally owned federal contracting companies owned by Cherokee Nation Businesses. As a trusted partner for more than 60 federal clients, Cherokee Federal LLCs are focused on building a brighter future, solving complex challenges, and **serving** the government’s mission with compassion and heart. To learn more about **CNSP** , visit cherokee\-federal.com.

We are mission and values driven and your contributions will make a difference. We make a positive difference in people's lives and help an average of 23 people per week to find a place to live.



If you join us, you will be able to advocate for change while also working with influential people who effect changes in policy and devote time to issues of racial and social justice. PATH is seeking candidates passionate about helping others make a positive change in their lives to join our Orange County Team as the Data Management Specialist, working out of our Costa Mesa office.


**ABOUT PATH**  

Since its foundation in 1984, PATH (People Assisting the Homeless) has pioneered bold and effective approaches to assist people experiencing homelessness. PATH operates services throughout California, connecting our clients to a comprehensive continuum of homelessness prevention, street outreach, employment preparation and placement assistance, individualized case management, supportive services, interim housing, and permanent supportive housing.


**ABOUT THE DATA MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST**  

As part of the Orange County Team, the Data Management Specialist is primarily responsible for supporting the work of PATH's CES Administration Team in collaboration with the County of Orange, as the Coordinated Entry System (CES)  

Lead Agency, HMIS agencies housing and service providers to connect individuals, families and survivors experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness to housing and appropriate housing interventions.



Position Responsibilities include:


* Carryout data management and system maintenance work, including program creation, modification, and regular updates (user access, account creation, termination submission).
* Implement program\-specific quality assurance processes in compliance with contractual obligations, confidentiality rules related to personal identifying information, and donor guidelines.
* Perform operational tasks related to data monitoring, data integrity, and quality control, focusing on data quality, ensuring compliance with standards, validating submissions, and accounting for correction.
* Assist in developing data management protocols and procedures, providing regular and timely updates.
* Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of agency\-wide databases, including HMIS (Homeless Management Information System) Clarity.
* Maintain compliance with CES policies and procedures, referrals through CES and compliance with HUD regulations.
* Maintain comprehensive and accurate record keeping along with comprehensive program assessments.


**WHAT YOU BRING**  

We're looking for candidates with:


* Analytical Skills and Attention to Detail: Gather and interpret data, identifying trends, patterns, and insights to inform decision\-making. Ability to consistently produce high\-quality work, ensuring accuracy and precision in all tasks.
* Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with others, seeking out and building positive working relationships with colleagues, participants, and stakeholders. Work effectively with others, contributing to team goals and recognizing the strengths and contributions of others.
* Communication: Convey information clearly and effectively (both verbally and in writing) to individuals and groups in a manner that informs, engages and maintains their attention.
* Creativity and Initiative: Take action and make decisions without being prompted, demonstrating a proactive approach to work and a willingness to take on additional responsibilities. Think outside the box, generating innovative solutions to problems or challenges.
* Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Analyze and evaluate information and situations, identify key issues, consider alternatives, and make logical decisions based on sound reasoning that will achieve the desired outcome.
* Ethics and Boundaries: Maintain ethical and professional standards, demonstrating honesty, integrity, and a commitment to doing the right thing in all situations while maintaining professional boundaries.


**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**


* Master's degree in related field
* Experience with HMIS, social services, or nonprofit administration, specifically regarding HUD funded programs.
* Four (4\) years of experience in a related job function or industry such as data management, program evaluation, research, and non\-profit program administration.


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**


* Bachelor's degree in related field
* Two (2\) years of experience in a related job function or industry such as data management, program evaluation, research, and non\-profit program administration


**MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS**  

Regardless of qualifications, candidates must:


* Have employment eligibility verification

jobs.description:

We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support \- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.

For 150 years, Watts has built best\-in\-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting\-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.

jobs.title: Pacific NW Habitat Restoration Specialist
jobs.description:
Overview/ Job Responsibilities:

Entarian is seeking a **Pacific Northwest Habitat Restoration Specialist** to provide technical, programmatic, data management, environmental compliance, outreach, and restoration planning support for the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation, Restoration Center. This position will support habitat restoration projects and related NOAA programs and initiatives in the Pacific Northwest, with a near\-term emphasis on the Community Based Restoration Program (CRP) and additional support to Damage Assessment, Remediation, and Restoration Program (DARRP) cases. The position requires periodic on\-site meetings in Portland, OR, and regional site visits and meetings with partners throughout Oregon, Washington, and Idaho, with regular off\-site work acceptable. The contractor may be required to travel for meetings, workshops, trainings, and conferences.  

Duties include:
Support fishery habitat restoration planning and implementation, including the evaluation, identification, prioritization, design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects, with particular emphasis on salmon and steelhead habitat and other biological resources in the Pacific Northwest.  

* Provide technical and programmatic support for CRP and DARRP restoration projects, including coordination with NOAA staff, local partners, state and federal trustees, responsible parties, technical professionals, and other stakeholders to support project development, implementation planning, monitoring, adaptive management, and reporting.
* Support project solicitation, review, and tracking activities, including distribution of requests for proposals, review and scoring of proposals, participation in technical review discussions, development of monitoring plans, participation in implementation planning, review of progress reports, and tracking of project accomplishments.
* Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible\-party restoration projects, including coordination of draft restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring and evaluation plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
* Support Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA) planning and stewardship activities, including gathering information from state and federal trustees, supporting case strategy and decisions through literature and expert\-opinion research, preparing topic papers, supporting use of settlement funds, and applying an integrated watershed\-based approach to restoration portfolios.
* Provide programmatic management support by coordinating and inspecting field activities and contract deliverables; supporting subcontractor oversight; identifying potential contract deviations; and providing technical input to the NOAA Project Lead and COR without exercising technical direction or final contract acceptance authority.
* Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA documentation using established NOAA and CEQ methods and guidance; Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act; and documentation needed to support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Endangered Species Act and Magnuson\-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.
* Develop outreach and communication products, including draft press releases, project fact sheets, briefing packets, maps, story maps, and other materials; and support public meetings, events, and other outreach activities as needed.
* Perform data management and reporting activities, including compiling and inputting project data into the Restoration and Conservation Database (RCDB), DARRTS, and other reporting databases; coordinating information requests; and working with the IT team on potential process improvements.
* Provide subject matter expert support to other NOAA programs and initiatives, including independent environmental resource and management studies, meeting participation and reporting, document development, engagement with topic experts, and literature reviews.

  

The salary for this position is approximately $69,000 \- 89,000/year.  

Periodic on\-site meetings in the Portland, OR office and regional site visits and meetings with partners throughout the Pacific Northwest (Oregon, Washington, and Idaho) are required, with regular off\-site work acceptable. The contractor may be required to travel for meetings, workshops, trainings, and conferences.
Minimum Qualifications:
* Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of four years of specialized professional experience in applicable field activities, methods, and practices related to habitat restoration, fisheries, ecology, aquatic sciences, or a related field.
* Knowledge of biological sciences and techniques pertaining to ecology, marine and anadromous fisheries, offshore and coastal aquatic habitat, invasive species, and Pacific Northwest biological resources.
* Demonstrated knowledge of salmon and steelhead habitat in the Pacific Northwest.
* Previous restoration project experience demonstrating knowledge of wetland restoration, fish passage techniques, and the application of ecological principles to habitat restoration.
* Demonstrated ability to perform field monitoring and habitat assessment activities to identify and evaluate habitat restoration projects.
* Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations related to living marine resources and habitat restoration projects.
* Familiarity with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
* Strong organizational and project management skills, including project scheduling, budgeting, tracking, reporting, and handling multiple concurrent and competing responsibilities.
* Experience with government document retention requirements.
* Experience working in a litigation\-sensitive environment.
* Strong oral and written communication skills.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
**Overview**

Vernadero Group Inc. (Vernadero) is a Veteran\-Owned Small Business founded in 1999 to provide infrastructure and environmental program support to Federal agency projects and activities throughout the United States and its territories. Vernadero is seeking a GIS Analyst to provide geospatial support for the Army National Guard (ARNG).

The successful candidate will join a team of other highly skilled analysts and will be responsible for performing geodatabase maintenance, quality control, and tool development on Common Installation Picture (CIP) layers. Typical responsibilities extend to web\-GIS, including maintenance and development of various ArcGIS Enterprise items including dashboards, hosted feature services, and scripting using the ArcGIS API for Python. The candidate must have some experience with nearly the entire ArcGIS suite of software because the position also requires leading training sessions and providing ad\-hoc support to ARNG staff and State/Territory GIS teams. This is a full\-time, permanent position that allows for remote teleworking.

Candidates who reside in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan region and are willing to work at least one day a week at the Army National Guard’s Readiness Center (TARC) facility in Arlington, Virginia, will be given precedence. The position also requires a Tier 1 Department of Defense background check and the ability to obtain a government issued Common Access Card.

**General Qualifications**

Candidates should possess the following minimum qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree in geography, geospatial science, computer science, or related field
* Minimum of 4 years of professional geospatial and geodatabase experience
* Extensive experience with ESRI ArcGIS Pro and utilizing extensions including data reviewer, spatial analyst, and network analyst
* Experience with ArcGIS Enterprise and manipulating/creating various types of items including dashboards, hosted feature services, and experience builder applications
* Experience with scripting using both ArcGIS Arcade, the ArcGIS arcpy module, and the ArcGIS API for Python
* Knowledge of Microsoft Office software, to include Excel, PowerBI, PowerAutomate, SharePoint, and Forms
* Excellent written and oral communications skills including leading training sessions and public speaking on occasion
* Customer service\-oriented skills to help with training sessions for entry\-level GIS users on how to pre\-process geodatabase submissions and use published map templates
* Organizational skills and the ability to work in a complex environment
* U.S. citizenship and ability to intermittently travel nationwide
* Valid U.S. driver’s license

**Preferred Qualifications**

Preference will be given to candidates that possess:

* Graduate degree in geography, geospatial science, computer science, or related field
* GISP Certification
* Experience leading GIS and geospatial support training classes
* Knowledge of Microsoft Access databases and how to update and maintain them
* Experience with Army and ARNG geospatial databases, infrastructure, and real property data and terminology
* Demonstrated experience with Python scripting using any ESRI\-published module
* Experience with SDSFIE version 4\.0
* Experience with the Department of the Army databases and software packages
* Experience administering an ArcGIS Enterprise Portal and PostgreSQL database

**Responsibilities** 

Specific responsibilities for the GIS Analyst may include the following:

* Develop content and teach GIS workshops to ARNG stakeholders
* Generate maps and other content to support funding requests for military construction projects to Congress via the DD 1391 process
* Communicate directly with ARNG stakeholders in multiple states
* Work with a team of GIS Analyst in the development of Common Installation Picture (CIP) data layers, metadata, and SDSFIE migration of several terabytes of data
* Maintain ArcGIS Enterprise dashboards, that include complex data sources involving Arcade scripting.
* Continued maintenance on a suite of ArcGIS Toolbox features including models, and published geoprocessing tools (Python arcpy module)
* Track stakeholder requests using various Microsoft SharePoint Lists and Excel files.
* Geodatabase quality control and post\-processing of ARNG stakeholder\-submitted data. This involves both manual and automated QA/QC procedures.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $80,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off

Work Location: Remote
